'''Adriana Elisabeth Hoffmann Jacoby''' (29 January 1940 – 20 March 2022) was a [[Chile]]an [[botanist]], [[environmentalist]] and author. She was executive secretary of Chile's [[National Environment Commission (Chile)|National Environment Commission]] ({{Langx|es|Comisión Nacional del Medio Ambiente}}, CONAMA) from 2000 to 2001. She advocated for the [[sustainable forest management|sustainable management]] and protection of Chilean forests, leading opposition to [[illegal logging]] in her role as coordinator of Defensores del Bosque Chileno (Defenders of the Chilean Forest) since 1992.

Hoffmann authored over a dozen books on the [[flora of Chile]], as well as 106 botanical names, mostly realignments of species and infraspecific taxa of [[cactus]].<ref name="EED">{{cite book |title=Environment Encyclopedia and Directory 2010 |publisher=Routledge |year=2009 |isbn=978-1-85743-377-7 |edition=5th |location=London |page=565}}</ref>

==Biography==
Adriana Hoffmann was born in [[Santiago]] to [[Lola Hoffmann|Lola]] (''née'' Jacoby) and Franz Hoffmann in 1940.<ref name=lifebio>{{cite book|chapter=Adriana Hoffmann|title=Homeostasis: Un Continuo Movimiento de Adaptacion|year=2013|publisher=Random House Mondadori|isbn=9789562583923|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=rcOZAAAAQBAJ&dq=%22adriana%20hoffmann%22%201940&pg=PT80|editor=Monsalve, Felipe|language=Spanish}}</ref> She grew up in [[Providencia, Chile|Providencia]] and attended [[Liceo Manuel de Salas]].<ref name=lifebio/> She was accepted at the [[University of Chile]] where she initially studied [[agronomy]].<ref name=lifebio/> She joined her mother when she traveled to Germany to study [[Psychiatry|psychiatric]] techniques and there Adriana changed her focus to [[biology]] and specialized in botany and [[ecology]].<ref name="Retiro"/> After she finished her studies, she returned to Chile and married engineer Hernán Calderón.<ref name="Retiro"/> They lived abroad for a time until returning to Chile in the 1970s.<ref name="Retiro"/>

Through her career, Hoffmann traveled throughout Chile, documenting flora and describing species.<ref name="EED"/> By April 2008, she had identified and classified 106 new cactus species.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Wakild|first=Emily|title=Environmental Justice, Environmentalism, and Environmental History in Twentieth-Century Latin America|journal=History Compass|date=February 2013|volume=11|issue=2|page=168|doi=10.1111/hic3.12027|url=https://www.academia.edu/2779220|access-date=11 January 2014|archive-date=31 March 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230331212006/https://www.academia.edu/2779220|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 1992, Hoffmann became coordinator of the non-profit organization ''Defensores del Bosque Chileno'', Chile's largest forest protection group.<ref name="UACh"/> She formed ''Agrupación de Defensores del Bosque Nativo'' in 1994, a group whose founding members included well-known singers and poets as well as economist [[Manfred Max Neef]] and Bishop [[Bernardino Piñera]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Clapp|first=Roger Alex|title=Waiting for the Forest Law: Resource-Led Development and Environmental Politics in Chile|journal=Latin American Research Review|year=1998|volume=33|issue=2|pages=24–25|doi=10.1017/S002387910003822X |jstor=2504061}}{{subscription required}}</ref> By the mid-1990s, Hoffmann was recognized as one of Chile's premier environmental activists.<ref name="KR">{{cite news|last=Ellison|first=Katherine|title=Pro-nature movement fights on despite foes and lack of funds|url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-17287111.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140610220725/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-17287111.html|url-status=usurped|archive-date=10 June 2014|newspaper=Knight-Ridder Newspapers|date=25 August 1995|via=[[HighBeam Research]]|url-access=subscription|quote=Some experts go so far as to say that Chile's 'green' activism boils down to just one high-powered woman: biologist Adriana Hoffmann, 55, head of Defenders of the Chilean Forest.}}</ref>

Hoffmann served on the board of the ''Lahuen Foundation'', a forest preservation organization that established ''El Cañi Sanctuary''.<ref>{{cite web|title=El Cañi Sanctuary|url=http://www.theconservationlandtrust.org/eng/el_cani.htm|publisher=The Conservation Land Trust|accessdate=9 January 2014|archive-date=18 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181018142737/http://www.theconservationlandtrust.org/eng/el_cani.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="who">{{cite book|title=The International Who's Who 2004|year=2003|publisher=Europa|location=London|isbn=978-1-85743-217-6|page=[https://archive.org/details/internationalwho2004ond/page/740 740]|url=https://archive.org/details/internationalwho2004ond|url-access=registration|quote=Adriana Hoffmann.|edition=67th|chapter=Hoffmann, Adriana}}</ref> She also played a leading role in the Chilean Science Society, Biology Society of Chile, Earth Foundation, [[International Union for Conservation of Nature]], and the Association of Chilean Female Leaders.<ref name="who"/> Hoffmann's efforts with ''Defensores del Bosque'' included developing [[environmental education]] programs for teachers.<ref>{{cite news|last=Moreira|first=Julio César|title=Profesores Aprenden a Proteger la Naturaleza|url=http://diario.elmercurio.com/detalle/index.asp?id=%7Bced24e9f-740d-4408-86ce-19668e0a4edb%7D|newspaper=El Mercurio|date=27 August 1999}}</ref>

Hoffmann was appointed by President [[Ricardo Lagos]] in March 2000 to serve as executive secretary of the [[National Environment Commission (Chile)|National Environment Commission]],<ref name="Retiro"/> a precursor of Chile's [[Ministry for the Environment (Chile)|Ministry for the Environment]]. During her tenure she oversaw the creation of the national [[hiking in Chile|hiking trail]] network [[Sendero de Chile]], improved the System of Environmental Impact Assessment (SEIA), and worked to implement environmental education programs and improve air quality in Santiago.<ref>{{cite news|title=Adriana Hoffmann renunció a la dirección de la Conama|url=http://www.emol.com/noticias/todas/2001/10/16/68681/adriana-hoffmann-renuncio-a-la-direccion-de-la-conama.html|newspaper=Emol.com|date=16 October 2001|access-date=11 January 2014|archive-date=5 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305013549/http://www.emol.com/noticias/todas/2001/10/16/68681/adriana-hoffmann-renuncio-a-la-direccion-de-la-conama.html|url-status=live}}</ref> During her tenure she encountered criticism from business interests for her environmentalist stances and from environmental groups for her perceived lack of influence within the administration.<ref>{{cite news|last=Checa|first=Laureano|title=Adriana Hoffmann dice que la lucha contra el cuoteo político fue mortal|url=http://diario.elmercurio.com/detalle/index.asp?id=%7B56a67161-4c35-404c-b288-e69d234d7611%7D|newspaper=El Mercurio|date=18 April 2002|language=Spanish}}</ref> Following the controversial approval of [[petcoke]] for gas-fired generators over her objections,<ref>{{cite news|title=CONAMA Director Hoffmann Facing Severe Criticism|url=http://santiagotimes.cl/conama-director-hoffmann-facing-severe-criticism/|newspaper=The Santiago Times|date=4 October 2001|access-date=11 January 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140111071917/http://santiagotimes.cl/conama-director-hoffmann-facing-severe-criticism/|archive-date=11 January 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> Hoffmann resigned in October 2001, stating that she no longer felt she was supported by Lagos or the Ministers.<ref name="UACh"/> She returned to work with ''Defensores del Bosque'' and prepared for her eventual retirement.<ref name="Retiro"/>

Hoffmann died on 20 March 2022.<ref>[https://www.latercera.com/nacional/noticia/fallece-la-biologa-y-botanica-chilena-adriana-hoffmann/55UMGMDETBG4NJ7CLRL2C54WMQ/ Fallece la bióloga y botánica chilena Adriana Hoffmann] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220320165205/https://www.latercera.com/nacional/noticia/fallece-la-biologa-y-botanica-chilena-adriana-hoffmann/55UMGMDETBG4NJ7CLRL2C54WMQ/ |date=20 March 2022 }} {{in lang|es}}</ref><ref name="CNNChile-Obit">{{cite news |title=A los 82 años falleció Adriana Hoffmann, la botánica reconocida como gran defensora de los bosques en Chile |url=https://www.cnnchile.com/pais/fallecio-adriana-hoffmann-botanica-defensora-bosques_20220320/ |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=CNN Chile |date=20 March 2022 |language=es |trans-title=At the age of 82, Adriana Hoffmann, the botanist recognized as a great defender of forests in Chile, passed away |archive-date=21 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220321012122/https://www.cnnchile.com/pais/fallecio-adriana-hoffmann-botanica-defensora-bosques_20220320/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Langman |first1=Jimmy |title=Adriana Hoffmann, pioneering Chilean environmental leader and botanist, dies |website=www.patagonjournal.com |date=21 March 2022 |url=http://www.patagonjournal.com/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=4394%3Amuere-adriana-hoffmann-pionera-ambientalista-y-botanica-chilena-&catid=78%3Amedioambiente&Itemid=268&lang=en |access-date=22 March 2022 |archive-date=22 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220322152735/https://www.patagonjournal.com/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=4394:muere-adriana-hoffmann-pionera-ambientalista-y-botanica-chilena-&catid=78:medioambiente&Itemid=268&lang=en |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Environmental advocacy==
During Pinochet's dictatorship, the government gave multinational [[timber]] firms unfettered access to Chilean forests and little incentive to process the lumber in-country.<ref name="MM"/> Hoffmann has noted that the rapidly disappearing private [[native forest]]s are mostly wasted through exports of wood chips.<ref name="E">{{cite news|last=Langman|first=James|title=Thinking Big|url=https://www.questia.com/read/1G1-19926794|newspaper=E Magazine|date=1 September 1997|access-date=7 January 2019|archive-date=8 December 2019|via=[[Questia]]|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191208103015/https://www.questia.com/read/1G1-19926794|url-status=dead}}</ref> In a 1995 article she remarked: "We've seen with our own eyes how [timber companies] take immense trees and shred the whole thing, branches and all."<ref name="MM">{{cite news|last=Lowy|first=Maxine|title=Shredding Chile's Forests|url=https://www.questia.com/read/1G1-17958635|newspaper=[[Multinational Monitor]]|date=1 November 1995|access-date=7 January 2019|archive-date=8 December 2019|via=Questia|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191208103011/https://www.questia.com/read/1G1-17958635|url-status=dead}}</ref> Beginning with her involvement with ''Defensores del Bosque'', Hoffmann agitated for the reform of [[Forestry in Chile|Chilean forestry]] practices.<ref name="MM"/> She was a vocal advocate for [[sustainable forest management]] in the country, arguing that [[ecotourism]] and value-added products like furniture lead to greater long-term revenue.<ref name="E"/>

Hoffmann wrote columns about ecology for ''[[El Mercurio]]'' in the 1990s<ref>{{cite web|last=Hanning |first=Sascha |title=El legado ecológico de Adriana Hoffmann |url=http://www.ciudadzen.com/sustentabilidad/medio-ambiente/ahoffmann/ |publisher=Ciudad Zen |accessdate=10 January 2014 |language=Spanish |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140111072435/http://www.ciudadzen.com/sustentabilidad/medio-ambiente/ahoffmann/ |archivedate=11 January 2014 }}</ref> and opposed free trade agreements that would replace native forests with commercial [[tree farm|tree plantations]].<ref name="Latinamerica Press"/> She criticized the Chilean government for not adopting a forestry policy.<ref name="Latinamerica Press">{{cite news|first=Hugo Godoy|last=Leon|title=Chile: Government Lacks Environmental Policy|url=https://www.questia.com/read/1G1-101533513/chile-government-lacks-environmental-policy|newspaper=Latinamerica Press|date=9 May 2003|access-date=7 January 2019|archive-date=8 December 2019|via=Questia|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191208103018/https://www.questia.com/read/1G1-101533513/chile-government-lacks-environmental-policy|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Hoffmann befriended American businessman and [[preservationist]] [[Douglas Tompkins]], who provided funding for ''Defensores del Bosque''.<ref name=nythero/> She defended his efforts to establish a 1,200-acre nature reserve in the [[Chilean Lake District]].<ref name=nythero/> ''[[The New York Times]]'' reported that she said: "If this investment were anywhere else but Chile, Mr. Tompkins would be considered a hero. But it happened in Chile, where envy and jealousy and business interests are institutions."<ref name=nythero>{{cite book|last=Spooner|first=Mary Helen|title=The General's Slow Retreat: Chile After Pinochet|year=2011|publisher=University of California Press|location=Berkeley|isbn=978-0-520-26680-3|page=111|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PtGSocthwq4C&dq=Adriana%20Hoffmann&pg=PA111}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Hoffmann was recognized by the [[United Nations]] in 1997 as one of the 25 leading environmentalists of the decade for her efforts to protect Chile's forests.<ref name="Retiro">{{cite news|first=Pilar Navarrete |last=Michelini|title=El retiro de Adriana Hoffmann|url=http://diario.elmercurio.com/detalle/index.asp?id=%7B2d3e6f87-93ad-4716-8d17-d89e5086caea%7D|newspaper=El Mercurio|date=10 December 2013|language=Spanish}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Perera|first=Victor|title=He Saves the Rain Forest by Buying It|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1997-03-16-op-38822-story.html|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|date=16 March 1997|access-date=11 January 2014|archive-date=11 January 2014|archive-url=https://archive.today/20140111063343/http://articles.latimes.com/print/1997-03-16/opinion/op-38822_1_chilean-forest|url-status=live}}</ref> For her research into Chilean flora and her work in environmental education, Hoffmann received the Luis Oyarzún Award from the [[Austral University of Chile]] in 2003.<ref name="UACh">{{cite web|title=Con motivo de 49 Aniversario: Universidad Austral de Chile Entregará "Premio Luis Oyarzún" a Adriana Hoffmann|url=http://noticias.uach.cl/principal.php?pag=noticia-externo&cod=870|publisher=Noticias UACh|date=2 September 2003|language=Spanish|access-date=11 January 2014|archive-date=3 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303202608/http://noticias.uach.cl/principal.php?pag=noticia-externo&cod=870|url-status=dead}}</ref> She received a Fellow Award from the [[Cactus and Succulent Society of America]] in 2009.<ref>{{cite web|last=Staples |first=Chuck |title=CSSA Fellows |url=http://cssainc.com/index.php/directory/honors/cssa-fellows/ |publisher=Cactus and Succulent Society of America |date=25 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131229031707/http://cssainc.com/index.php/directory/honors/cssa-fellows/ |archivedate=29 December 2013}}</ref>

Hoffmann served on the judging panel for the [[United Nations Environment Programme]]'s Sasakawa Prize.<ref>{{cite web|title=A Renctas Na Mídia |url=http://www.renctas.com/pt/informese/renctas_brasil_detail.asp?id=214 |work=Four of a Kind – Part 2 |publisher=BBC |date=15 May 2005 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140111081205/http://www.renctas.com/pt/informese/renctas_brasil_detail.asp?id=214 |archivedate=11 January 2014}}</ref>

==Works==
Hoffmann authored more than a dozen books and illustrated field guides on the flora, medicinal plants and botanical resources of Chile.<ref>{{cite news|last=Purto|first=Mauricio|title=El legado de Adriana Hoffmann|url=http://diario.elmercurio.com/detalle/index.asp?id=%7B7e21f411-2b2d-4627-8381-799ccd4c5b3f%7D|newspaper=El Mercurio|date=26 July 2008|language=Spanish}}</ref> Among her works was ''La Tragedia del Bosque Chileno'', which includes text and photographs that document [[illegal logging]] in Chilean forests.<ref>{{cite news|last=Aguirre|first=Andrés|title=Ecología|url=http://diario.elmercurio.com/detalle/index.asp?id=%7B2e03acf4-ac70-4619-86ea-cb71acaeef4f%7D|newspaper=El Mercurio|date=28 August 1999}}</ref>
